positive.prompt: Apply the coding standards to this backend module: no raw strings, typed ids and enums, errors as domain objects, defensive code only at the edges
Review this TypeScript code for strict typing, low cyclomatic complexity, injected dependencies, and comments that only explain the why
Quick one-line fix in the payment handler, what coding rules do I need to follow before I commit
Refactor this Python service so JSON is typed at every boundary, illegal states are unrepresentable, and no secrets are in source

negative.prompt: Model the domain for orders: bounded context, aggregates, domain events, and typed ids
Write a backward-compatible migration with rollback and update the drawdb schema

evals.prompt: Here is a TypeScript order service where status is a string, the handler catches and logs errors, Date.now() is called inline, and every function starts with null checks. Bring it up to the coding standards.
evals.expected_output: A rewrite where the status is an enum or literal union, errors surface as a typed error union, the clock is an injected provider, validation moves to the API edge, and each change cites the C rule it satisfies
expectations: The string status becomes an enum or literal union and ids become branded types (C1, C2)
No error is caught and swallowed; errors are a typed error union per module (C15, C16)
Date.now() and any inline dependency construction are replaced by injected providers (C19)
Null checks inside business logic move to the edge or become a first-class domain object with an explicit error (C3, C11)
Any comment that narrates what the code does is removed; a why comment carries the ticket id (C21)
